event.title: Trump Issues Threats Against Iranian Infrastructure Amid Strait of Hormuz Tensions
event.canonical_title: Trump Issues Threats Against Iranian Infrastructure Amid Strait of Hormuz Tensions
event.summary: US President Donald Trump has threatened to target Iranian bridges and power plants in retaliation for any attacks on ships in the Strait of Hormuz. He stated that for each ship fired upon by Iranian forces, the US would respond by destroying a corresponding piece of Iranian infrastructure. This escalation comes amid ongoing tensions in the region and rising oil prices.

event_overview.title: About Iran War
event_overview.subject: Iran War
event_overview.summary: The Iran War refers here to the ongoing international armed conflict involving Iran, the United States and Israel, with military operations and diplomatic efforts centered on Iran and extending to maritime security in the Persian Gulf, Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea. The conflict has also drawn in regional actors and affected commercial shipping and energy markets, while its legal and political basis remains a subject of dispute among the parties and within the United States.

facts.label: Conflict chronology
facts.value: A U.S. notification to the UN described Israeli action beginning on June 13, 2025 and reported that U.S. forces struck Iran’s Fordow, Natanz and Isfahan nuclear facilities on June 22, 2025; it characterized these actions as part of an international armed conflict.

facts.label: 2026 U.S. operations
facts.value: In a March 2026 letter to the UN Security Council, the United States said it began combat operations on February 28, 2026, alongside Israel, citing protection of U.S. forces and regional partners and the free flow of maritime commerce through the Strait of Hormuz.

facts.label: Geographic and commercial significance
facts.value: The Strait of Hormuz lies between Iran and Oman and links the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman and Arabian Sea; it is a major route for petroleum and liquefied-natural-gas exports.

facts.label: Energy-market exposure
facts.value: The U.S. Energy Information Administration estimated that petroleum and other liquids transiting Hormuz averaged 4.9 million barrels per day in the second quarter of 2026, down from 21.6 million barrels per day in the fourth quarter of 2025 before the conflict.

facts.label: U.S. legal and congressional framework
facts.value: The War Powers Resolution requires a written report within 48 hours when U.S. forces are introduced into hostilities or certain combat-equipped foreign deployments without a declaration of war; it is the framework under which Congress considers measures concerning U.S. involvement in Iran.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline focuses on late-July 2026 escalation, congressional war-powers activity, threats to maritime and energy infrastructure, Houthi-linked attacks and ceasefire diplomacy; it does not provide a complete account of the conflict’s origins, all military operations, humanitarian effects or negotiations.
